<!-- Generated by release/scripts/cli_reference/build.py from schemas/dist/openapi.yaml. Do not edit; run `make cli-reference`. -->

Taken before the command word (`blowhorn <flag> <command>`) and by every command:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--pace` | string |  | Pace of the random delays between actions, accepted by every blowhorn command and before the command word as well ('blowhorn --pace slow post ...'): a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set). Commands that never sleep accept it and say so in their own --help |

Taken by most commands; a command's own page lists any it describes differently:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--chrome-launch` | string |  | How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension) |
| `--config` | string |  | Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml) |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | `false` | Simulate execution without making changes |
| `--exclude`, `--e` | string |  | Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults |
| `--headed` | boolean | `false` | Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge |
| `--headless` | boolean | `false` | Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once |
| `--log-dir` | string |  | Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console |
| `--profile` | string |  | Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles) |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | boolean | `false` | Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY) |

Exit codes, unless a command's page lists its own:

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | The command failed; with --json, stdout is a Problem (\`ok: false\`, \`error\`). |
| `2` | Usage error: an unknown flag or a bad argument (Click). |
| `3` | The store is unavailable (\`EXIT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE\`); with --json, stdout is a Problem. |
